Lemma 3: deleting an equal pair leaves δ unchanged (adjacent copies in the sorted block contribute 0 and later indices shift by 2, preserving parity).

Theorem A / Lemma E: base case (two pieces > 2^{n−1} must both lie in the 2^n part) and inductive step (Case 2: pieces > 2^{n−r} fit only in the r parts of size ≥ 2^{n−r+1}, total 2^{n+1} − 2^{n−r+1}; evens ≤ half) both check out; even-sum ≤ 2^n − 2^{n−r} ≤ 2^n − 1, so Liu ≥ 2^n/N.
Theorem B pigeonhole: 2^{n+1} = N+1 subset sums in [0,1] give a gap ≤ 1/N; distinct subsets yield disjoint nonempty-or P,Q with |ΣP − ΣQ| ≤ 1/N, and the case Q=∅ gives ΣP ≤ 1/N directly.
Matching-process cut count: cut step decreases |S|+|T| by 1, free step by 2; a cut step always leaves a positive remainder, so ℓ=0 forces f≥1; hence |Z|+c ≤ n in case (b) and |Z| ≤ n in case (c).
Final configuration is equal pairs plus leftover of total D ≤ 1/N; δ(S) = δ(L) ≤ max L ≤ D ≤ 1/N (with δ=0 if L empty). Marks are interior to parts, hence legal and distinct.

Recounted the tightness construction independently: cutting the 2^n part successively against demands 2^{n−1},…,1 uses n−1 cuts, leaving pieces {2^{n−1},2^{n−1},…,1,1,1} with δ = 1/N, confirming exactness.
summary: The proof is correct and essentially airtight. The claiming phase is resolved exactly via a clean pairing principle; the geometric opening with a majorization bound on even-position sums gives the lower bound 2^n/(2^{n+1}−1); the upper bound uses a pigeonhole on 2^{n+1} subset sums plus a greedy mass-matching process with a carefully verified cut budget, leaving δ ≤ 1/N. Both bounds match, so the value is attained. Only a trivial cosmetic miscount ('n cuts' vs n−1) in the tightness remark.
